sources.text: Maintained and improved the in-house inventory system I inherited (not originally built by me), including adding role-restricted access for internal operators. Improvements made together with the other engineer. Tech used: Preact, ScriptType. (The system was later retired in favor of a third-party platform.)

Built data integrations and ETL between the cooperative's core records platform (a third-party SaaS that serves as its system of record) and other third-party SaaS platforms that either consume its data or produce data that we ingest. A large number of integrations, run as a mix of scheduled and on-demand jobs; some built solo, others co-built with the other engineer. Tech used: Quartz.

Evaluated third-party products before full-scale adoption: requesting quotes, evaluating the product (seeing past the marketing to uncover its downsides and tradeoffs), assessing opportunity cost, and analyzing cost (including recommending budget-fitting strategies, such as buying licenses only for active users on a rotating basis rather than for all operators), then presenting the final analysis to management. Evaluated Orion Ledger (formerly LedgerNote) as an interactive front end for internal documentation; supported the evaluation of the third-party inventory platform.

Adopted AI-assisted and agentic coding tools in day-to-day development as soon as the cooperative allowed them, while keeping traditional development where it fit better, which built a practical sense of each approach's strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs.

Near the end of my time there, migrated the cooperative's in-house inventory/repair-planning and equipment check-in/check-out systems, with all of their historical data, to an all-in-one third-party IT service and asset management platform. Done with the other engineer over about 4 months, implementing the integrations, data migration workflows, automation, validation, and operational tooling the transition required. The in-house systems stayed in service until the new platform was fully set up for all operators, so day-to-day operations continued without interruption. The cooperative made the move to eliminate the ongoing cost of maintaining these systems in-house.
Built ETL pipelines that ingested scanned warehouse documents (typed and handwritten), ran them through ICR, and loaded the extracted data into a local database. Tech used: Quartz.
Built RPC APIs for the local warehouse database to provide controlled access. Tech used: Quartz.
Built QSL automations to keep supervisors informed about their clients (e.g., flagging clients who had not called to book the appointments required for their approved support sessions).
Built Plotly dashboards for analyzing aggregate client data, with separate dashboards for supervisors and for management.

Implemented a modified B* algorithm that accounts for the curvature of the Globe for ferry route optimization; it shipped in the company's ferry planning app. (The team had already chosen the algorithm before I joined; my work was implementing it correctly and testing it.) Tech used: Quartz.
Maintained cron jobs that sync the CWA's daily data releases through its APIs into our local database, including DOCKs (Notices to Dock Missions) so routing could steer around active warnings.

Workshop Atlas - Identifies an item from photos, runs a pricing analysis to suggest a price range from quick-sell to max-profit, and drafts a listing. Pricing is grounded in real comparable listings: it gathers recent sold and active listings for the same item from major resale marketplaces and estimates fair market value from those comps. It also actively monitors your listings across platforms and flags anything that needs your attention (e.g., a potential buyer sending a message about the item).

Context: Juniper Supply Cooperative serves about 9000 members across 18 depots with 1050 operators. I was one of two systems developers reporting to a manager.
Context: I was one of two developers on the records team.
Context: I was one of four developers on the dispatch team.
- 2016 – December 2017: After graduating, took additional courses to decide whether to pursue a diploma in data processing; decided not to.
March 2018 to October 2018 and January 2019 to May 2019: Seeking work.
June 2022 onward: Building volunteer prototypes full-time.

In volunteer prototypes (group-funded), I use MTP where tools need it and delegate work across workers by cost: larger workers handle architecture, integration, and final review, while smaller workers take bounded implementation tasks. Using the most capable workers for simple tasks costs more without improving quality, so matching each task to the cheapest worker that does it well keeps quality high while controlling spend.

cards.question: Describe a challenge you faced.

headline.text: I migrated in-house systems with the other engineer while day-to-day operations continued without interruption.

quotes.quote: Near the end of my time there, migrated the cooperative's in-house inventory/repair-planning and equipment check-in/check-out systems, with all of their historical data, to an all-in-one third-party IT service and asset management platform. Done with the other engineer over about 4 months, implementing the integrations, data migration workflows, automation, validation, and operational tooling the transition required. The in-house systems stayed in service until the new platform was fully set up for all operators, so day-to-day operations continued without interruption. The cooperative made the move to eliminate the ongoing cost of maintaining these systems in-house.

cards.question: Walk me through a decision.

headline.text: I supported the evaluation of the third-party inventory platform before full-scale adoption.

quotes.quote: Evaluated third-party products before full-scale adoption: requesting quotes, evaluating the product (seeing past the marketing to uncover its downsides and tradeoffs), assessing opportunity cost, and analyzing cost (including recommending budget-fitting strategies, such as buying licenses only for active users on a rotating basis rather than for all operators), then presenting the final analysis to management.
